actions.action: Commit the update and delivery receipt together
actions.mechanism: A unique event receipt and business update share one transaction; acknowledgement follows successful commit.
actions.implementation: Insert a receipt keyed by partner and event ID. Only the successful inserter applies the update. On conflict, skip it and acknowledge.
actions.check: Crash before commit, after commit before acknowledgement, and during acknowledgement; replay concurrently. Verify exactly one committed business update.
actions.risk: External side effects require a transactional outbox and downstream idempotency.

actions.action: Guard entity updates with monotonic revisions
actions.mechanism: Atomic revision comparisons prevent stale events from replacing newer entity state, independently of event-ID deduplication.
actions.implementation: Within the receipt transaction, condition replacement updates on stored revision being lower. For dependent deltas, reject gaps without committing receipts; reconcile first.
actions.check: Deliver revisions 12, 10, 12 concurrently under distinct IDs; replacement state must finish at 12. Verify gapped deltas remain unapplied.
actions.risk: Skipping revisions is safe for replacement snapshots, not necessarily incremental changes.

actions.action: Expire receipts conservatively within a measured storage budget
actions.mechanism: Seven-day retention from first durable receipt covers redelivery without extending retention on every duplicate.
actions.implementation: Keep receipts through first-seen plus seven days; delete only strictly afterward. Serialize cleanup with receipt handling. Measure all durable deduplication storage; backpressure before 2 GB.
actions.check: Replay just before and exactly at expiry: no repeat. After expiry, verify cleanup and stale-revision protection. Load-test one million 64-byte IDs including indexes.
actions.risk: Seven days must bound arrival delay; longer delays need longer retention or permanent revision protection.
